description: Hi everyone, this is Arjun. Astronomy and astrophysics are one of my fav fields! This solo team helps to address fire safety concerns within space to ensure the next big leap for mankind is much safer. We are doing the Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data challenge to help use the powers of SI to benefit fire safety amongst space missions.
summary:
I built Nova Ember, an AI/SI-powered dashboard to help analyze and assess flames in microgravity using NASA PSI (Physical Sciences Informatics) datasets and mitigate fire safety risks in space, helping make the next big leap safer.

We integrate SI (Super Intelligence/AI) into data from NASA PSI and related research across 35+ investigations, including FLEX, BASS-II, and Saffire, to help scattered information be analyzed, processed, and used to assist fire safety without manually searching across multiple sources.

You can ask the AI agents to analyze the data using frontier models and translate raw PSI data into scientific insights. Nova Ember can summarize, rank, and interpret combustion findings and compare investigations side by side, helping researchers explore material flammability, flame spread rates, and extinction limits.
details:
This is Nova Ember, an AI/SI-powered dashboard to help analyze and assess flames in microgravity using NASA PSI (Physical Sciences Informatics) datasets and mitigate fire safety risks in space, helping make the next big leap safer.

We integrate SI (Super Intelligence/AI) into data from NASA PSI and related research across 35+ investigations, including FLEX, BASS-II, and Saffire, to help scattered information be analyzed, processed, and used to assist fire safety without manually searching across multiple sources.

The project intends to help increase our present understanding of flames in microgravity and various environments. Nova Ember helps improve fire prevention, detection, and suppression by making relevant research easier to find and understand.

This solution uses the OpenAI Responses API for AI/SI intelligence inference, which powers the research agents, while combining semantic and keyword search to find relevant information based on your query or factors. Nova Ember uses OpenAI’s embedding model to represent research text as vectors. PostgreSQL’s pgvector extension stores and searches those vectors to find passages relevant to a user’s question, which the AI agents can then use to support their answers and help power various features of your dashboard, including agentic AI. In addition, the primary core languages used are HTML, Python, and TypeScript. This is how it functions: React, Next.js, and TypeScript power the frontend, while Vega handles the charts and Three.js handles the 3D objects and visualizations. Our backend uses Python FastAPI, with PostgreSQL powering the memory and stored datasets. It also has a Python worker for longer research, processing, and exports. The awesome part is Nova Ember is open source under Apache 2.0!

Finally, our creativity comes from the unique AI approaches: combining semantic and keyword search to find relevant evidence, agentic AI, and custom agent capability, alongside preserving scientific honesty and accuracy. In addition, we include multiple PSI experiments such as, but not limited to, FLEX, BASS-II, Saffire, FLARE, SAME, and SAME-R. We considered several factors throughout the hackathon, including scientific accuracy and rigor, possible reduction in hallucination and false information by introducing strict safeguards to responses, and finally, a good, digestible UI/UX that helps a person, so it is understandable whether they are an undergraduate or graduate student, professor, aerospace researcher, or engineer.

Live demo: https://nova-ember.duckdns.org/app
